# Ops error sweep — BASELINE MARKER

**BASELINE: swept through 2026-08-12T04:00Z.** The next sweep should use that as its start.

## Baselines used — this was a COLD START

No prior AWS-or-Actions ops error sweep exists anywhere in the ticket store. A search for "error sweep" returns 219 tickets, but every one is a *code* sweep (observability floors, lint sweeps, docs sweeps) or an unrelated session_log. `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md` covers the code-health audit, not an operational log sweep.

**Therefore a 7-day window was used and this is stated as an assumption, not a measurement:**
- AWS: 2026-08-05T00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T04:00Z
- GitHub Actions: 2026-08-05T00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T03:30Z

## AWS findings (account 896586841071, us-east-1 — read-only calls only)

Account confirmed as rebar own: `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` notes rebar shares its account with the decommissioned `snap` demo, and both `snap-demo-*` and `rebar-*` resources are present.

**Structural note for the next sweeper:** there are **no Gerrit/review-bot CloudWatch Log Groups**. The only log groups are Lambdas (`lmn-*`, `snap-demo-*`), all of which returned **zero** ERROR/Exception/Traceback/FATAL matches in the window. The Gerrit box publishes **custom metrics** (`rebar/host`, `Rebar/Gate`) from journald via the host observability probe instead. So `filter-log-events` is the wrong tool here — **alarm history + metric datapoints are the log surface**.

All 13 `rebar-*` alarms were OK at sweep time. Five ALARM episodes in window, all self-clearing:

| Alarm | Episodes | When (PDT) |
|---|---|---|
| rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts | 3 | 08-07 04:33, 08-07 05:55, 08-11 20:08 |
| rebar-gerrit-voter-errors | 2 | 08-05 07:32 (18 seconds), 08-06 21:17 (5 min) |
| rebar-root-disk-pressure | 1 (cleared) | cleared 08-06 02:27 |

Zero datapoints all week for `deploy_errors`, `g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`, `review_bot_merge_change_errors`; no dips in `reviewbot_healthy` or `gerrit_healthy`.

**Bedrock:** ~77 InvocationClientErrors, ~94% on the Nova family (nova-pro took 50 in one hour on 08-10 22:00 PDT). Fully explained by e800 (Nova 10k output ceilings), now closed and landed. The Claude ladder saw 1-3 each, which is why the client-error alarm correctly stayed OK. 17 InvocationServerErrors clustered 08-11 10:00-12:00 PDT are provider-side. Quantified in a comment on b902.

## GitHub Actions findings

| Workflow | failure | cancelled | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gerrit Verified Gate | 103 | 95 | Expected churn — in-flight changes during a bug bash; aggregated only, logs not read |
| Reconcile Bridge | 12 | 255 | **12 real** (filed 9a71); 255 cancellations **benign** |
| Test Suite (mirror) | 8 | 1 | 2 flakes, 2 fixed, 1 unreproducible |
| Reconciler Heartbeat Canary | 6 | 4 | **True-positive alarms**, downstream of the bridge stalls |
| Mirror Guard | 3 | 4 | 1 transient replication lag; 2 runner cancellations |
| Live External Integration | 1 | 0 | **Real** — commented on 10c3 |
| Dependabot / Optional-Dep / CodeQL | 1 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 1 / 1 | Benign |

Zero non-success runs for reconcile-bridge-canary, dependency-advisory-canary, terraform-drift, prompt-eval, structured-output-baseline, jira-dc probes, release, lockdown, verify-identity.

**The 255 Reconcile Bridge cancellations are benign and should not be re-investigated.** `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` sets `concurrency: {group: reconcile-bridge, cancel-in-progress: false}`, and the continuous loop re-dispatches itself, so the group is occupied nearly always. GitHub holds at most one pending run per group, so each new `*/20` cron run supersedes the previously queued one. Every sampled cancelled run has **jobs=0** and a ~3-minute created->updated span — it never allocated a runner. 247 of 255 are `schedule` events. This is designed behavior (and the reporting question was already settled by closed task 03ef) — but it does make the Actions failure feed hard to read.

**Known flakes checked and NOT present** in this window on any non-Gerrit workflow: the complexity-baseline shallow-clone race, and the alert_dedup collection error (fixed by change 1606).

## Tickets filed (3 new bugs)

- **9a71-ba9b-89d0-4cb8** (sole-curbable-stinkpot) — Reconcile Bridge ACLI auth expiry + mid-pass `command cancelled`, 12 failures over 6 days, stalled the bridge 6.5h on 08-07. Top signal of the sweep.
- **b8b1-6462-b4f1-4a1d** (censorian-goldleaf-cicada) — reconciler re-attempts structurally-impossible links every pass; never converges, permanent log noise floor. Linked `relates_to` 9a71.
- **7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9** (greasy-plucky-piranha) — autodeploy review-interrupt alarm fired 3x in 7 days post-34cd; deferral run-up implies `bound-exceeded`, but the metric has no dimensions so the journald reason field must be checked to confirm.

## Tickets commented (3 existing)

- **c89f-08b1** — 4 new occurrences of the xdist worker crash, all py3.11, all 08-08, self-resolved after.
- **10c3-5a33** — first LIVE occurrence of the lost-write-on-lock-timeout outside a contention test; broke reconciler idempotency in the Jira DC suite.
- **b902-18af-14ed-4da1** — Bedrock error quantification from the Nova model-comparison runs.

## Not filed, with reasons

- **Bridge fsck keyset envelope drift** (macos py3.13, 08-11): **passes on current main** — verified by running `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py` locally (3 passed). Likely fixed by a subsequent landing or platform-specific. Not filed.
- **review-bot health payload key rename** (`in_flight` -> `queue_depth`, 08-08) and **mypy MCP camelCase kwargs** (08-07): both one-off, both fixed the same day.
- **Mirror Guard divergence** (08-07 14:16): single transient Gerrit->GitHub replication lag.

## Caveats on this sweep

- No shell access to the Gerrit host, so journald was never read — the autodeploy interrupt reason is inferred from metric shape only (see 7b4a).
- Gerrit Verified Gate logs were deliberately not read (198 non-success runs of expected bug-bash churn); a real defect hiding in that volume would have been missed.
- One tracker write hit a 60s flock timeout mid-sweep and was retried successfully — itself an incidental sighting of the 10c3/9305 contention family.

No code was changed. All AWS calls were read-only.
